scope: Isolated Godot 4.7.2 GL Compatibility benchmark. One deterministic 900x520 encounter is shown simultaneously in two 684x395 viewports, each at 684x395 output size. Side-on compresses world depth; elevated three-quarter exposes more world Y. Both panels receive the same simulation coordinates, source hero, combat state and controls. This is a diagnostic blockout, not the game build.
purpose: Compare readability of player/torch silhouette, enemy attack telegraph, battlefield route and Purple Haze footprint with camera perspective as the intended variable.

design_contract.player_fantasy: Wayfarer torchbearer reads a rival rogue's wind-up, sweeps the Haze lantern through the close threat, places a persistent ground-area field and dodges the strike.
core_loop: read the orange wind-up marker and attack lane
sweep torch for a range-checked hit
cast a persistent Haze field that damages an enemy inside its radius
dodge during the strike's invulnerability window

camera_modes.side_on: world Y compressed 0.18 around shared combat floor
camera_modes.elevated: world Y compressed 0.70 around arena center

acceptance: Both cameras receive identical scenario inputs and preserve health/combat results
torch strike lands once on a foe in its range
Haze persists and applies at least one area tick
enemy wind-up/strike occurs during dodge invulnerability without damage
both captures show the same hero source and route landmark
Godot Compatibility runtime has no script/engine errors

hero_source_concept.use: source for one fused cutout presentation image; not runtime sprite animation

hero_runtime_cutout.approval: feasibility cutout only; alpha halo/shadow/smoke remain; explicitly rejected as rig source

assets_and_provenance.enemy: Original runtime blockout drawing used only for scale, lane and telegraph testing; not production character art.
assets_and_provenance.environment: Original in-engine Cinderwild geometric blockout; not final background art.

runtime.renderer: GL Compatibility / OpenGL 3.3 NVIDIA 610.78 NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti Laptop GPU
runtime.assertion_note: Deterministic automated smoke applies the same actions/state handlers as input; the locomotion phase includes 0.90 seconds at +250 units/s, a reversal, then movement at -190 units/s until the dodge. Separate manual keyboard playtesting was not performed.

authored_animation_runtime_check.renderer: GL Compatibility / OpenGL 3.3 NVIDIA 610.78 NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti Laptop GPU
authored_animation_runtime_check.observed_result: Each mode passed: one torch hit, one Haze zone tick, one dodge, two enemy strikes, zero hits taken, hero health 3, rogue health 1; locomotion covered 324.25 world units with one direction reversal; no script or engine errors.
visual_features: phase-keyed attack anticipation, contact, follow-through and planted-foot recovery
alternating two-step walk cycle with counter-swinging arms, body bob and cloak drag
camera-depth comparison preserves upright actor anatomy in both projections
lantern hand/staff sweep, fire and embers timed to the action
Ash Rogue wind-up, strike and recovery silhouette with telegraph
persistent Haze lobes, curling wisps, source ribbon and remaining-duration bar
dodge compression, directional burst, recovery pose and cyan invulnerability motes
screen-spaced nameplates, action-state labels and hit confirmation

strengths: Upright character silhouettes retain head-to-foot proportions while their horizontal spacing remains easy to scan.
A low, lateral Haze footprint reads as a persistent screen-plane band and does not engulf the full vertical field.
tradeoffs: Depth and route width collapse toward a narrow ground strip; terrain depth and area-field shape are suppressed.
Large environment landmarks contribute less tactical information.

strengths: Route, landmark and field footprint occupy more vertical information space; path and Haze coverage are easier to reason about spatially.
Actor head-to-foot proportions remain upright while their projected ground positions reveal separation in depth.
tradeoffs: The elevated composition expands floor-plane information and can bring route/Haze marks closer to the characters; the blockout cannot establish production framing.
A small number of actors are insufficient to prove crowding, occlusion or target-selection behavior.

agent_visual_read.current_read: Both camera panels share the exact same encounter and outcomes. Locomotion now presents an alternating step cycle with visible foot lifts, counter-swinging arms and cloak drag; attack anticipation/contact/follow-through, dodge phases and rogue strike are timed to gameplay state. Actor anatomy stays upright while only world placement depth is compressed by camera mode. Side-on prioritizes action; elevated reveals route/Haze geography. All geometry, characters except the static idle reference, and effects remain diagnostic blockout presentation.

visual_review_limits: Hero locomotion, attack and dodge are procedural, anchored diagnostic poses synchronized to gameplay timers; they are not sampled source frames or a production sprite rig. Idle uses the fused static identity reference.
Ash Rogue remains a diagnostic blockout, despite its phase-driven wind-up, strike, recoil and telegraph.
Environment projection and haze footprint are diagnostic camera compositions, not a calibrated production camera or volumetric effect.

No separate human playtest, production-game integration, performance measurement, full viewport/device/aspect-ratio matrix, or accessibility audit has been completed. Paired output captures were smoke-tested at 1440x900 (16:10) and 1600x900 (16:9); broader viewport coverage remains open.
Environment shapes and hand-drawn combat/Haze effects remain temporary diagnostics, not production art or final effects.
remaining_gate: Integrate approved production layered/rigged hero and enemy art plus the production Haze effect; test real traversable collision/layout and complete manual/aspect-ratio/device review; obtain human review before final camera or art lock.

aspect_ratio_review.status: Paired runtime smoke and output captures verified at 1440x900 (16:10) and 1600x900 (16:9); fixed panels fit at both tested sizes. Evidence: aspect-captures/aspect-ratio-review.json. 4:3, OS-scale, alternate-device, manual-playtest and production-camera gates remain open.
